newsitem.title: USA: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/VIX softens as indices drift.
newsitem.headline: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/VIX softens as indices drift.

text.p: Implied volatilities for U.S. stock index options softened in the morning as the stock market drifted in relatively narrow ranges after Tuesday's big rally that soothed fears of a major bear market, traders said.
"They're taking premiums out all over the floor now," said Jesse Stamer of TradeNet, a designated primary market maker at the Chicago Board Options Exchange.

He said April options were the hardest hit because they expire on Friday and have steep time decay, adding that the market during April expiration weeks had tended to be choppy on a daily basis but little changed on the week.
The CBOE volatility index .VIX, which reflects implied volatilities for near-month S&P100 index .OEX options, was off 0.47 point at 20.37 at 1135 CDT/1635 GMT, with the OEX off 0.63 at 734.78.
Still, traders said the high gamma in the Aprils was attracting bullish speculators seeking quick premium acceleration.
Open interest in April 735 and 740 calls had actually increased slightly on Tuesday, and those contracts were also two of the three busiest OEX options today with almost 10,000 lots each trading.
"There's such an overwhelming amount of pessimism in the market that you can't expect there to be too much more downside pressure," he noted.

He said the 10-day moving average for CBOE equity put/call ratio stood at a relatively high level of about 0.54, with Tuesday's single-day ratio marking 0.58 despite the market's rally -- a positive signal for contrarians who view interest in puts as a bullish factor.
Such put/call ratio levels often preceded a major market rally, although the effect of a tighter credit stance by the U.S. Federal Reserve remained to be seen, Oyster said.
